instruction:
The starting input is `/home/user/Desktop/broken.fst`, which references complete but intentionally faulty `broken_elasto.dat` and `broken_inflow.dat` modules plus a version-matched dependency closure. Only initialization inputs are preloaded; generate all result artifacts yourself.

The OpenFAST executable is `/home/user/miniconda3/bin/openfast` when working on `broken.fst`. Complete a diagnose-fix-rerun workflow using only the command line: 1. Run `openfast broken.fst`, read the terminal or echo diagnostics, repair one reported input fault at a time, and rerun until all faults are identified. Retain the first failed run as `/home/user/Desktop/diagnostic_1.log` and the post-NumBl second failed run as `/home/user/Desktop/diagnostic_2.log`; these logs must preserve the real OpenFAST diagnostics in order. 2. Save the corrected modules as `/home/user/Desktop/fixed_elasto.dat` and `/home/user/Desktop/fixed_inflow.dat`; save a `/home/user/Desktop/fixed.fst` that explicitly references both corrected modules. Do not bypass them by referencing another baseline module. 3. Run `fixed.fst` through 60 s and retain `/home/user/Desktop/fixed.out` and save its normal-termination console output as `/home/user/Desktop/normal_termination.log`. 4. Write `/home/user/Desktop/postprocess.py` to compute the complete `GenPwr` series arithmetic mean and maximum, and save `/home/user/Desktop/fixed_summary.txt` as `mean_pwr_kw, max_pwr_kw`. 5. Write `/home/user/Desktop/diagnosis.txt` with at least 100 English word tokens, explaining every actual error message, root cause, field, old value, corrected value, and verification. 6. Do not use GUI tools.
